claim: Todai-ji Great Buddha Hall admission is 800 yen adults / 400 yen children 6-12, with a 1,200 yen joint pass for hall plus museum; open 7:30-17:30 Apr-Oct and 8:00-17:00 Nov-Mar.
quote: April-October: 7:30 - 17:30 November-March: 8:00 - 17:00 ... Individual tickets for the Great Buddha Hall cost 800 yen for adults ... A joint pass covering both the hall and museum is available at 1,200 yen for adults.

claim: Todai-ji's Daibutsuden is one of the world's largest wooden buildings and houses Japan's largest bronze Buddha (Daibutsu), a UNESCO World Heritage temple worth 60-90 minutes.
quote: Todaiji ... is one of Japan's most famous and historically significant temples ... Its main hall, the Daibutsuden (Big Buddha Hall) is the world's largest wooden building, despite the fact that the present reconstruction ... is only two thirds of the original ... houses one of Japan's largest bronze statues of Buddha (Daibutsu).

claim: Kasuga Taisha, founded as Nara's tutelary shrine and patron shrine of the Fujiwara clan, is famous for hundreds of bronze hanging lanterns and stone lanterns lining its approaches; the paid inner area costs 700 yen.
quote: The lanterns are only lit twice a year during two Lantern Festivals, one in early February and one in mid August ... visitors can pay 700 yen to enter a paid inner area for closer views of shrine buildings displaying distinctive Kasuga architectural style.

claim: Kasuga Taisha's outer precincts are free to enter; March-October hours are 6:30-17:30 and November-February 7:00-17:00, reachable by bus to the Kasuga Taisha Honden stop.
quote: Entry to the outer precincts is free, and the inner Honden costs 500 yen. Hours: March to October: 6:30 AM to 5:30 PM, November to February: 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

claim: Kofuku-ji's five-story pagoda is undergoing its first major repair in ~120 years from July 2023 until March 2034, during which it is fully covered by a temporary roof and scaffolding, so the famous silhouette is not visible.
quote: Kofukuji's 5-storied pagoda is undergoing extensive renovation works from July 2023 until March 2034, during which the pagoda is covered up ... a major preservation and repair project - the first in approximately 120 years - has now begun.

claim: Kofuku-ji is a UNESCO World Heritage temple whose National Treasure Hall displays the celebrated three-faced Asura statue, a masterpiece of Nara-period sculpture.
quote: In 1998, Kofuku-ji was recognized as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara' ... The National Treasure Hall displays a wealth of cultural assets, including the renowned Asura statue, a masterpiece of Nara period sculpture.

claim: Isuien Garden, a traditional Japanese strolling garden, is open 9:30-16:30 and closed Tuesdays; the 1,200 yen adult ticket also covers the Neiraku Museum.
quote: Isuien is open 09:30-16:30, closed Tuesdays. Admission is 1,200 yen for adults ... and this includes both gardens and the Neiraku Museum.

claim: Yoshikien Garden is open 9:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30) and is free to foreign visitors on showing a passport, while Japanese nationals pay 250 yen.
quote: Yoshikien Garden is usually open from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with last entry at 4:30 PM. Foreign visitors receive free admission (show passport at entrance), while Japanese nationals pay 250 JPY.

claim: Nara National Museum specializes in Japanese Buddhist art, is open 9:00-17:00, closed Mondays, with free entry for visitors aged 18 and under.
quote: The museum is basically open from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The museum is closed on Mondays ... Free of charge entry is available to people aged 18 years or younger and high school and below.

claim: Nara Park's free-roaming sika deer (protected as a Natural Monument) number a record 1,465 in 2025 and are famous for bowing to receive shika senbei crackers sold at 200 yen per bundle of ten.
quote: The deer population in Nara Park has risen to its highest ever number of 1,465 in 2025 ... These crackers cost 200 yen for a bundle of ten ... made of wheat flour and rice bran ... they get shika senbei upon bowing their heads.

claim: Horyu-ji is the world's oldest wooden construction and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, about 20 minutes on foot from JR Horyuji Station in Ikaruga.
quote: Founded by Shotoku Taishi, Horyuji Temple is the oldest wooden construction in the world... Approximately 20 minutes on foot from JR Horyuji Station

claim: Horyu-ji adult admission is 1,500 yen, covering all main precincts; it sits about a 30-minute train ride from Nara City.
quote: Adults (over 12 years old) pay 1,500 yen, while elementary and junior high students pay 750 yen, with the fee covering access to all main precincts.

claim: Yakushi-ji in the Nishinokyo area is a UNESCO temple roughly 1 minute walk from Kintetsu Nishinokyo Station, open 9:00-17:00 with 1,000 yen adult admission, and its 8th-century East Pagoda is the only surviving original structure.
quote: About 1 minute walk from Kintetsu-Kashihara Line's Nishinokyo Station... admission is 1,000 yen for adults... The East Pagoda (Toto) stands out as the only original 8th-century structure that has survived, completed in 730 CE

claim: Toshodai-ji, founded by the priest Ganjin, is a UNESCO temple about 8 minutes walk from Kintetsu Nishinokyo Station, open 8:30-17:00 with 1,000 yen adult admission, and a few minutes' walk from Yakushi-ji so the two are easily combined.
quote: From Yakushiji Temple, it is just a few minutes walk to World Heritage Toshodaiji Temple, which has a very different atmosphere... admission: adults 1,000 yen

claim: Naramachi is Nara's former merchant district of preserved Edo-period machiya townhouses, 10-15 minutes walk south of Kintetsu Nara Station, worth about half a day for shops, cafes, Gangoji Temple and the free Koshi-no-Ie lattice house (open 9:00-17:00, closed Wednesdays).
quote: Koshi-no-Ie Residence is a former merchant home open to the public... Admission: Free... Plan on spending half a day exploring the Naramachi area... Naramachi is located about a 10-15 minute walk to the south of Kintetsu Nara Station.

claim: Mount Wakakusa (342m) is open from the 3rd Saturday of March to the 2nd Sunday of December, 9:00-17:00, costs 150 yen for adults, takes about 30 minutes to hike to the summit, and offers panoramic views of Nara City including Todai-ji and Kofuku-ji plus a top-three night view of Japan.
quote: Adults (middle school students and up): 150 yen... Open from 3rd Saturday of March to second Sunday of December... Approximately 30 minutes from the mountain's base to reach the peak... named one of the 'New Three Major Night views of Japan'

claim: The Wakakusa Yamayaki mountain-burning festival is held on the 4th Saturday of January; in 2026 it falls on January 24 with fireworks at 18:15 and ignition at 18:30.
quote: Wakakusa Yamayaki is a festival held on the 4th Saturday of January every year. The festival will be held on Mt. Wakakusa on January 24, 2026 (Saturday), and fireworks are at 18:15, with the mountain ignition at 18:30.

claim: From Kyoto, Kintetsu express is 45 min / 760 yen and limited express 35 min / 1,280 yen, while JR Miyakoji rapid is 45 min / 720 yen.
quote: Express Train: 45 minutes, 760 yen; Limited Express: 35 minutes, 1,280 yen ... JR Miyakoji Rapid Service: 45 minutes, 720 yen

claim: Kintetsu Nara Station is an underground station a few steps from Kofukuji and Nara Park, while JR Nara station is a 15-20 minute walk west of the park; Kyoto JR is 720 yen and Kintetsu 760-1,280 yen.
quote: an underground station just a few steps from Kofukuji and Nara Park ... the JR station is a 15-20 minute walk west of Kofukuji and the park

claim: From Osaka-Namba, Kintetsu Rapid Express is about 39 min / 680 yen and limited express 34 min / 1,200 yen; JR Yamatoji rapid from Osaka Station is 45 min / 840 yen and covered by the JR Pass.
quote: Rapid Express train takes 39 minutes and costs 680 yen ... Limited Express services take 34 minutes and cost 1,200 yen ... Yamatoji rapid ... one-way trip takes 45 minutes, costs 840 yen

claim: A pack of 10 shika senbei deer crackers costs 200 yen and a portion of the proceeds goes to activities to protect the park's deer.
quote: A pack of 10 deer biscuits costs 200 yen ... A portion of the proceeds goes to activities to protect the park's deer.

claim: During the autumn rut (stags in heat Sept-Oct), 35 people were injured at Nara park in September 2024 (a 7-fold year-on-year rise), 10 needing hospitalization, mostly puncture wounds to the thigh.
quote: 35 people were injured in September 2024 ... 10 of those injured required hospitalization ... From September to October each year, the stags are in heat and become more aggressive

claim: Kofukuji halls and museum are open 9:00-17:00 (entry until 16:45) with grounds open 24 hours; individual halls cost 500 yen each, the National Treasure Museum 900 yen, or 1,600 yen combined.
quote: 9:00 to 17:00 (entry until 16:45) ... 900 yen (National Treasure Museum) 500 yen (Central Golden Hall) 500 yen (Eastern Golden Hall) 1600 yen (all three)

claim: Kasuga Taisha main sanctuary worship hours are 6:30-17:30 (Mar-Oct) and 7:00-17:00 (Nov-Feb), with a free offering hall and a paid inner area for a closer view.
quote: General Worship of Main Sanctuary: March - October 6:30 - 17:30, November - February 7:00 - 17:00

claim: A half-day Nara visit (~4-5 hours incl. train) covers the deer and Todaiji; a full day adds Kasuga Taisha, Naramachi and Isuien, with the forested Todaiji-to-Kasuga walk taking about 20 minutes.
quote: a comfortable half-day trip takes 4-5 hours including train travel ... The path from Todaiji east through the forest to Kasuga Taisha takes 20 minutes on foot

claim: Nakatanidou near Higashimuki Shopping Street sells yomogi (mugwort) mochi from 200 yen, open 10:00-19:00, famous for lightning-fast mochi pounding, no credit cards.
quote: Famous for its lightning-fast mochi pounding performances... the fragrance of mugwort with subtly sweet red-bean paste... Hours: 10:00am - 7:00pm... Price: 200 yen and up... Credit cards not accepted

claim: Nakatanidou's yomogi mochi is filled with tsubu-an and dusted with kinako; the shop has been a Tabelog Hyakumeiten (Top 100) honoree five times and holds a Guinness record for mochi-pounding speed; best chance to see pounding is noon to late afternoon.
quote: Yomogi Mochi is freshly pounded mugwort mochi filled with sweet tsubu-an and dusted with fragrant kinako... Tabelog Hyakumeiten (Top 100) shop five times... Guinness World Record for its mochi-pounding speed... best chance usually from around noon to late afternoon

claim: Nara specialties include kakinoha-zushi (salted mackerel/salmon on vinegared rice wrapped in persimmon leaves), Miwa somen (thin Sakurai wheat noodles), narazuke (1300-year-old sake-lees pickles), and Yoshino Hon Kudzu sweets like kuzumochi and kuzukiri.
quote: Mackerel or salmon are dipped in salt, placed on vinegared rice, and wrapped in fragrant persimmon leaves... Narazuke... Traditional pickle representing Nara with a history of over 1300 years... vegetables are soaked in sake lees... Yoshino Hon Kudzu, gathered in Yoshino region in southern Nara

claim: Harushika sake brewery (Imanishi Seibei) in Naramachi at 24-1 Fukuchiincho offers a five-sake tasting for 500 yen with a souvenir glass to keep; open 10:00-17:00 daily, cash-only, with a cafe serving light meals.
quote: Five different sakes for ¥500, with a souvenir glass to keep... 10:00 to 17:00 daily... 24-1 Fukuchiincho, Nara, approximately a 15-minute walk from Kintetsu Nara Station... shop operates on a cash-only basis

claim: Mizuya Chaya is a thatched-roof Taisho-era teahouse beside a stream between Todaiji and Kasuga Taisha in Nara Park, serving udon/soba in winter, shaved ice in summer, and traditional sweets, frequented by deer.
quote: thatched-roof cottage from the Taisho era... between Kasugataisha Shrine and Todaiji Temple... from hot udon and soba noodles in winter to shaved ice in summer, along with traditional sweets... frequented by friendly deer

claim: Yamato-cha is Nara green tea; Machiya Cafe Kanna in a 100+ year-old Naramachi merchant house serves a matcha chocolate fondue using Yamato tea, and GRANCHA in the Higashimuki Arcade specializes in Yamato matcha daifuku.
quote: Machiya Cafe Kanna is a charming Nara café housed in a more than 100-year-old merchant house in Naramachi... The Matcha Chocolate Fondue is a popular choice that features a special matcha sauce made with Yamato tea

claim: Higashimuki Shopping Arcade is a covered street next to Kintetsu Nara Station lined with about 80 stores including restaurants, food shops and clothing.
quote: Higashimuki Shopping Street is a covered arcade conveniently located next to Kintetsu Nara Station... lined with about 80 stores on both the east and west sides

claim: Mochiidono Arcade, one of Nara's oldest shopping streets, has over 70 shops including craft stalls selling tenugui by local Nara artists, Kawamoto Pottery Shop (80-year-old pottery store), and Haruhino selling handcrafted deer-leather goods.
quote: Mochiidono Arcade has over 70 shops... selling local crafted goods, including Tenugui... designs made by young artists who live in Nara... Kawamoto Pottery Shop... Haruhino sells beautifully made handcrafted leather goods... made of deer leather

claim: Nara is the birthplace of green tea consumption in Japan, with the first recorded use in 729; Yamato-cha is the local variety.
quote: Nara is particularly famous for green tea as it's the site where consumption of green tea in Japan was first recorded, in 729

claim: Nara cherry blossoms in 2026 opened around late March with peak full bloom in early April (around April 2-5).
quote: Cherry Blossom Reports 2026 - Nara: Approaching Full Bloom

claim: In 2026 Nara blossoms started opening around March 26 with peak viewing around April 2.
quote: blossoms are expected to start opening around March 26, with peak viewing around April 2

claim: Nara Park autumn foliage runs mid-November to early December, with ginkgo peaking around Nov 22 and maples around Nov 26 in 2025.
quote: 2025 Nara Autumn Foliage Update

claim: Kasuga Taisha held special illuminated nighttime worship on select November dates during the 2025 autumn foliage season.
quote: Nearby Kasuga Taisha... offers special nighttime events on November 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29, 2025, where you can see the main hall... lit for special worship.

claim: The Shika no Tsunokiri deer antler-cutting ceremony is held in mid-October at Rokuen deer garden in Nara Park during fall rutting season, in roughly 40-minute paid sessions to prevent injuries from aggressive bucks.
quote: originally established to prevent injuries during this period... Location: Rokuen (The deer garden) in Nara Park... Approximately 40 minutes per session, with 4-5 sessions daily

claim: The deer antler-cutting tradition dates back roughly 340 years to the Edo Period and is held annually at Rokuen near Kasuga Taisha.
quote: Centuries'-old deer antler-cutting ceremony returns to Nara

claim: The Wakakusa Yamayaki (Burning of Mt. Wakakusa) takes place January 24, 2026, with fireworks at 18:15 and mountain ignition at 18:30.
quote: The Yamayaki Festival 2026 will take place on Saturday, January 24, 2026... Fireworks are at 18:15, and the mountain ignition is at 18:30.

claim: The Omizutori ceremony at Nigatsudo Hall (Todai-ji) runs March 1-14, a 1,250-year-old Buddhist ritual featuring giant fire torches.
quote: The Omizutori ceremony takes place at the Nigatsudo Hall from March 1 to 14... the falling sparks from the torches are believed to protect onlookers

claim: The Nara Tokae lantern festival runs August 5-14, 2026, 7:00-9:30 PM, centered on Ukigumoenchi south of Todai-ji, free to view with a 500 yen donation to light a lantern.
quote: Dates: August 5-14, 2026... Times: 7:00 PM - 9:30 PM... centered around Ukigumoenchi, located south of Todaiji Temple

claim: Yatadera Temple opens its hydrangea garden of 10,000+ plants in 60 varieties from June 1 to July 10, peak rainy-season viewing, with 500 yen adult admission.
quote: Yatadera Temple opens its sprawling hydrangea garden from June 1st until July 10th each year... over 10,000 plants... Admission is 500 yen for adults

claim: Mount Yoshino's cherry blossoms bloom roughly 1-2 weeks later than central Nara due to higher elevation, with tens of thousands of trees in tiered groves.
quote: Mount Yoshino usually blooms 1-2 weeks later due to higher elevation

claim: Asuka Village's scattered archaeological sites (e.g. Ishibutai Kofun) are best explored by bicycle, coverable in 3-4 hours, reached via Kintetsu line to Asuka Station (~30-40 min from Nara).
quote: Cycling lets you cover them comfortably in 3-4 hours... From Kintetsu Nara Station, take the Kintetsu Yoshino Line south to Asuka Station

claim: Mount Koya is reached from Nara via Osaka (Namba/Shin-Imamiya) onto the Nankai Koya Line and cablecar; recommended as an overnight shukubo temple stay rather than a rushed day trip.
quote: From Nara take either the Kintetsu Nara Line to Namba Station... change to the Nankai Koya Line for Gokurakubashi Station... highly recommended as an overnight trip

claim: The official Nara tourism site lists Yatadera's hydrangea viewing period as early June to early July, over 10,000 shrubs, admission 700 yen adults / 300 yen children, located at 3549 Yatacho, Yamato-Koriyama, with extra buses from Kintetsu Koriyama station in June-July.
quote: over 10,000 hydrangea shrubs around Yatadera Temple ... Adults: 700 yen ... 3549 Yatacho, Yamato Koriyama ... Extra buses run from Kintetsu Koriyama station in June and July

claim: neoNARA confirms Yatadera holds roughly 10,000 hydrangeas in 60 varieties (peak May 25-June 30, 8:30-17:00, 700 yen, bus from Kintetsu-Koriyama to the Yatadera stop) and names other Nara hydrangea temples: Hasedera (3,000+, mid-June to mid-July), Okadera (~3,000), Hannyaji, and free Umami/Umakami parks (4,000).
quote: Approximately 10,000 hydrangeas in 60 varieties ... Peak viewing: May 25 – June 30 ... Hasedera Temple ... Over 3,000 hydrangeas ... Okadera Temple ... Approximately 3,000 ... Umakami Kyuryo Park: 4,000 hydrangeas; free admission

claim: A Nara local guide corroborates Yatadera as the premier June hydrangea spot (10,000 plants, 60 species, 700 yen) and lists other rainy-season draws: Umami Hillside Park irises as 'the key feature of June', fireflies near Nigatsu-do (8-9 p.m.), and a Rose Festival at Ofusa Kannon (May 15-June 30).
quote: an amazing 10,000 blooming plants of 60 different species ... Umami Hillside Park ... features irises as "the key feature of June" ... Fireflies ... around Nara Park near Nigatsu-do Temple ... Rose Festival: May 15–June 30 at Ofusa Kannon Temple

claim: Takidani Hanashobu Garden in Uda, Nara Prefecture is a dedicated iris (hanashobu) garden in a valley about 10 minutes' walk from Kintetsu Osaka Line's Sambonmatsu Station, with irises flowering in June.
quote: Takidani Hanashobu Garden ... Uda, Nara Prefecture ... about 10 minutes walk from Kintetsu Osaka Line station Sambomatsu ... irises ... flower in June

claim: Naramachi is a historic merchant district near Gangoji Temple preserving architecture from the Edo through postwar periods, about a 15-minute walk from Kintetsu-Nara Station.
quote: About 15-minute walk from Kintetsu-Nara Station, or about 20-minute walk from JR Nara Station to Gangoji Temple.

claim: Naramachi is a preserved Edo-era machiya district that developed on Gangoji Temple's grounds; the narrow-fronted townhouses arose because taxes were levied by house frontage.
quote: taxes were levied according to the frontage of the house

claim: Naramachi Koshi-no-Ie (Lattice House) is a free-admission reproduction of a traditional Naramachi townhouse, open 9 a.m.-5 p.m. and closed Mondays and New Year period (Dec 26-Jan 5).
quote: Admission free ... 9 a.m. - 5 p.m. ... a reproduction of a traditional townhouse in Naramachi

claim: Gangoji Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that once occupied most of the Naramachi area, charges 500 yen admission and opens 9:00-17:00; the free Lattice House is one of few machiya open to the public.
quote: The temple opens its doors to the public from 9:00 to 17:00 with a last admission at 16:30 throughout the year for a minor fee of 500 yen per person.
